title: Auth Control Plane workload token (v1 wire format)
description:
The workload token the auth-service signs for one internal service caller (credential class `workload_token`, TRD section 11): a compact JWS whose protected header and payload, decoded, are the two members of this document. The signature is not part of the document; a verifier checks it with the issuer's jwks.v1 key named by `kid`, and the signed bytes are decided by the golden corpus under golden/workload-token.

A workload token is its own type and its own shape. Its header typ is `workload+jwt` (RFC 8725 explicit typing), exact bytes, so it can never be read as a user access token (`at+jwt`), an ID token or the HS256 token (`JWT`). It names exactly one audience, a service from contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/audiences.json whose classes include `workload_token`. It has no `org_id`, no `sid` and no `scope`: a workload acts for no organization and no session, and nothing in it grants a permission. Its lifetime is at most 300 seconds (a client rule, WorkloadTokenLifetimeCeiling): a verifier refuses a longer one even when the signature is valid.

header.description: The JWS protected header. Closed: a verifier never reads a key, key URL or certificate from the token.

alg.description: Ed25519 only (ACP-ADR-01). A verifier fixes this before it resolves a key.

typ.description: RFC 8725 explicit type, exact bytes. A verifier refuses a case variant, a missing typ, `JWT`, `at+jwt` and an `application/`-prefixed form. It separates this token from the user access token (`at+jwt`).

claims.description: The JWT claims. Closed to the workload and its validity: no organization, no session, no scope, nothing that grants a permission.

aud.description: Exactly one audience: one service. contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/audiences.json lists every audience and the classes that may carry it; an audience whose classes lack workload_token is refused.

principal_type.description: A workload token names a workload principal. A human principal holds a user access token.

numericDate.description: Seconds since the epoch (RFC 7519 NumericDate), no later than 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z.
